newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends up, near top of two week range.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends up, near top of two week range.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended higher Thursday, in line with LME copper prices in London, with sentiment about the near term turning positive.
"We're seeing some pretty decent trade buying, after the back months firmed up recently and there's some expectation of a possible further fall in LME stocks Friday," one trader said.
COMEX December copper ended up 0.75 cent at 90.45 cents, after pushing up to two week highs at 91.20 cents intraday.
"Copper could continue to edge up toward technical objectives at 94 cents, although profit taking could quickly take prices back below 90 cents," CPM Group analyst Edward Kemp said.
The COMEX December/March backwardation widened a little to 1.00 cent, from 0.80 cent at Wednesday's close, after narrowing from 2.30 cent on August 30.
COMEX copper warehouse stocks rose 287 short tons Thursday to 21,819 short tons, but further falls in LME copper stocks are expected this week.
The fallout from the Sumitomo affair, which rocked the copper market mid-year now appears to be over, analysts said.

Most major players had now closed out most of their options positions, allowing banks to reduce their risks also, Deutsche Sharp Pixley Metals trader Richard Hirsche told delegates at the Institute of Srap Recycling Industries (ISRI) conference in Chicago Wednesday.
Mitsubishi Corp also believes the downside risk has eased for the copper market, the major trading house said in its latest monthly report Thursday.
